subject: Staggered accelerator + usage guardrail proposal for HelixAI renewal
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Staggered accelerator + usage guardrail proposal for HelixAI renewal

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the chat this morning. I pulled together a short proposal that tries to balance HelixAI’s desire for an aggressive uplift incentive with our need to keep unit economics predictable during a midterm scale. Key points in the attached:

- Staggered accelerator: incremental discount tiers that unlock as Helix commits additional reserved units (3 tiers: +20%, +50%, +100% over current). Each tier gives an additional rebate applied retroactively at next invoice.
- Usage guardrail: overages are capped and subject to a true-up rather than open-ended discounts — propose an overage cap at 120% of committed units with standard true-up billing.
- Early renewal credit: one-time invoice credit if customer signs amendment to co-term within 30 days of SOW.
- Pilot bucket: recommend a small burst bucket for immediate headroom while legal finalizes amendment.

I attached a simple workbook (staggered-accelerator-proposal-helixai.xlsx) with modeled scenarios. Please take a look and call out any constraints from procurement/legal on your side. If the structure looks acceptable we can draft a short amendment for co-term + uplift and route to legal.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm whether Helix prefers monthly vs quarterly invoicing for the top-up.
2) Procurement confirms PO window / approval cadence.
3) We schedule a brief follow-up (30m) to walk numbers with Ben and Aditya.

Thanks —

Laura Bennett
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference

Laura —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the model. A few clarifying questions from procurement/finance (Maya looped in):

1) Billing cadence: can we opt into monthly invoices for the top-up but keep core contract quarterly? We prefer more frequent reconciliation.
2) Early renewal credit: is that applied as an up-front credit on the next invoice or as a rebate after we hit the first tier? Also any expiry on that credit?
3) Overages: you mentioned a cap at 120% with true-up — can you clarify whether usage above 120% would be billed at list rate or subject to a higher overage multiplier? For us predictability matters.

If you can reply with specifics on those three items we can run through procurement and get an LOI out quickly.

Thanks —
Samir
VP, Ops & Finance
HelixAI

Hi Samir / Maya —

Quick answers to Maya's questions below. High-level: happy to give Helix the flexibility on cadence and to tighten predictability around overages.

1) Billing cadence: Yes — we can invoice the top-up monthly while keeping the underlying reserved commitment on a quarterly invoice schedule. Monthly invoicing for the top-up requires a short amendment to call out the invoice line and billing terms; we usually do net-30.

2) Early renewal credit: this is provided as a one-time invoice credit applied on the first post-amendment invoice (not a retroactive rebate). It is valid only if the amendment is signed within 30 days of the proposal date; credit amount depends on tier signed (see sheet). No additional expiry beyond standard invoice aging rules.

3) Overages: usage between 100% and 120% of committed units is billed at standard overage rate (list rate less the tier discount). Any usage beyond 120% will be billed at list rate without discount but subject to a true-up conversation — we do not apply a punitive multiplier by default. If Helix expects sustained >120% usage we should discuss moving them up a tier or converting usage to reserved units.

Ben attached an updated CSV with the monthly/quarterly invoice rows separated and a worked example for the 50% uplift case.

If Helix is comfortable with that, Laura and I can ask legal to draft an amendment with the pilot bucket and early-renewal credit called out. Also can offer a one-time 5% onboarding credit (applied as a billing credit) if Helix commits to co-term within 30 days and agrees to a 12-month minimum on the uplift.

-Ben

Subject: RE: Staggered accelerator + usage guardrail proposal for HelixAI renewal

Samir / Maya —

Thanks for the questions and for looping procurement in. To summarize the agreed path so there is no ambiguity:

- Billing cadence: Helix will be invoiced monthly for the top-up line; core reserved commitment stays on quarterly invoices.
- Early renewal credit: one-time invoice credit applied on the first invoice after amendment executes, valid if signed within 30 days.
- Overages: usage up to 120% billed at the discounted overage rate; beyond 120% billed at list rate (no automatic multiplier).
- Pilot bucket: Redwood will provision a small burst bucket (30 days) to give you headroom while legal finalizes the amendment.
- Add-on incentive: conditional one-time 5% onboarding credit if co-term executed within 30 days and 12-month minimum on the uplift.

Next steps:
1) I will ask legal to prepare a clean amendment first thing Monday and share a DocuSign link.
2) If Helix can provide a PO or LOI by Aug 14 we can lock March pricing into the amendment and provision the pilot bucket immediately.
3) Let's schedule a 30-minute handoff call tomorrow to walk the amendment language and invoicing rows (Ben / Aditya on the call).

Samir — can you confirm PO window and whether Maya prefers the handoff call at 10am or 3pm PT tomorrow?

Thanks —
Laura
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
